title: spec review: R4: orchestrator/concurrency.py — adaptive concurrency limit 0..hard_max from independence, critical path, capacity and merge pressure, with logged reasons (AP P13)
spec:
Why: daemon.dispatch fills wave_limit = min(slots, max_wave or slots) (orchestrator/daemon.py:690) — concurrency is always the hard maximum. AP P13 / brief P8 want a selected concurrency below the hard cap derived from evidence, never above it.
What: new pure module orchestrator/concurrency.py; no daemon edits.
- compatible_groups(ready_ids, pairwise_rows) -> list of lists: connected components over pairs with level hard or soft (rows shaped like interference.pairwise: {a, b, level, reasons}); singletons are independent tasks.
- select_limit(hard_max, ready_ids, tasks, pairwise_rows, priorities, snapshot=None, pressure=None, durations=None, cfg=None) -> {"hard_max", "limit", "reasons": [strings], "tasks_considered": ready_ids, "expected_benefit_s", "groups": n_groups}. Rules, each appended to reasons when it binds: no ready work -> 0 ("no_ready"); limit starts at hard_max ("hard_max=N"); independent bound: at most one task per compatible group, so limit <= number of groups ("compatible_groups=k"); coupled group of size >= 3 with only hard edges -> limit 1 for that group ("coupled_group:<ids>"); shared-interface or migration reasons (reason kinds interface, migration, same_glob, glob_covers) -> conservative: limit <= max(1, groups-1) ("shared_interface"); capacity bound from snapshot: sum of executor free (or claude_workers_free in fallback) ("capacity=m"); pressure saturated -> limit <= max(1, independent singletons) ("merge_pressure=saturated"); cfg concurrency_mode = "fixed"|"adaptive" (default adaptive; fixed returns hard_max with reason "fixed"); minimum 1 when ready work exists and capacity > 0. Never exceed hard_max.
- expected_benefit_s = sum(est durations of the first `limit` ranked tasks) - max(those) using durations dict or critical_path.est_duration_s priors.
- log_row(result, wave_ids=None) -> dict ready for schedlog.append('concurrency', ...) with keys hard_max, limit, reasons, tasks_considered, expected_benefit_s, selected (wave_ids), observed_outcome None.
acceptance: tests/test_concurrency.py::test_coupled_group_selects_low_concurrency — four ready tasks all pairwise hard-coupled yield limit 1 with a coupled_group reason
tests/test_concurrency.py::test_independent_modules_select_higher_concurrency — five ready tasks with no interference and hard_max 4 yield limit 4 and reason hard_max binds
tests/test_concurrency.py::test_hard_max_is_never_exceeded — twenty independent tasks and hard_max 3 yield limit 3
tests/test_concurrency.py::test_no_ready_work_yields_zero — empty ready set yields limit 0 and reason no_ready

tests/test_concurrency.py::test_quota_and_merge_pressure_bound_the_limit — snapshot with 2 free executor slots bounds limit to 2 with a capacity reason; pressure saturated with one independent task bounds to 1 with merge_pressure=saturated; log_row carries hard_max, limit, reasons, tasks_considered, expected_benefit_s

risks.issue: select_limit's 'coupled group of size >= 3 with only hard edges -> limit 1' rule is applied as a single global scalar limit, so any one hard-coupled cluster in the ready set forces the entire wave to 1 even when other independent compatible_groups exist and are ready. This directly contradicts P13's own example ('five independent modules -> higher') and defeats the goal of the module. The only acceptance test for this rule (test_coupled_group_selects_low_concurrency) has zero independent groups present, so the conflict with independent work is never exercised.

The spec's shared-interface rule keys on reason kinds 'interface' and 'migration', neither of which interference.classify ever produces (hard kinds are dependency/same_file/glob_covers/same_glob; soft kinds are dir_contains/same_dir/test_adjacent/sibling_globs/graph_link). As written the branch is only reachable via same_glob/glob_covers, which are already hard edges folded into compatible_groups/coupled_group, so this rule is effectively dead code against real pairwise_rows and no acceptance test covers it.

Spec's Why cites 'brief P8' for the concurrency-selection motivation, but P8 is 'Scout result structure' (unrelated). The relevant sections are P13 (Adaptive parallelism) for the core rule and P11 (Merge-pressure awareness) for the merge_pressure signal.

suggested_spec_changes: Clarify whether the coupled-group-size>=3 rule should throttle only that group's contribution (e.g. cap it at 1 within compatible_groups accounting, letting other groups still count toward limit) or is intentionally meant to serialize the whole wave whenever any large hard cluster is ready; add a test mixing one coupled cluster of 3+ with several independent singletons to pin down the intended behavior.

Drop 'interface' and 'migration' from the shared-interface reason-kind list (or mark them explicitly as reserved for a future interference.py extension not yet implemented), and add an acceptance test that exercises the shared_interface bound using reason kinds interference.py actually emits (same_glob/glob_covers) at group size 2.
Fix the Why line to reference P13 (and P11 for merge_pressure) instead of P8.
